about: Far terrain around the real-size Santa Monica: USGS 3DEP 1/3" (ned10m via OpenTopoData) on land, OSM coastline (ODbL) for land/sea. Frame: g(lat,lon) of scratchpad/venice/proj.py (LAT0 34.0100, LON0 -118.4960, axis 134.8 deg, skew K .00923, +222 s, +42.5 t); s = m inland (NE-ish), t = m along coast (NW negative). This is the UNSHIFTED real frame: it matches the city grid (SMD.E) (checked at 31 nodes: median 0.1 m, worst 2.2 m, at the top of the bluff) but NOT south.json south of t 600 (game s = frame s - C_south(t)), and the real coast is not at s 0 outside the city (see coast). Heights in m above sea, rounded to 0.5; sea nodes are 0.

grid.note: 300 m over the whole view, row-major (row = t). Inside 25 km of (600,-1000) and on Palos Verdes every node is sampled; beyond that only every other node (600 m) is sampled and the rest filled with the mean of the nearest sampled 600 m nodes (3448 nodes).

sea_note: run lengths over grid.h order, alternating, first run = land (0), then sea (1), ...; sea = seaward of the OSM coastline

fine.note: 150 m, every node sampled: Topanga/Pacific Palisades/Santa Monica Canyon/Brentwood/Mandeville/Getty/Bel Air/Westwood and the city. Use instead of grid inside its box.

coast.note: s of the mainland water line (most seaward OSM coastline crossing along +s) every 100 m of t; null where the row has none. RAW: jumps at harbour mouths and headlands (e.g. 336 m between t 5900 and 6000 at Marina del Rey); smooth it (e.g. running median over 1 km) before using it to warp. game s = s - coast(t) puts a spot the right distance from its own beach.
